subject: Short-lived trace preservation for production debug (FinProd) - workflow & approvals
messages:
From: Luke Barnes <luke@finprod.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: support@finprod.com
Date: 2027-04-22T09:15:00Z
Subject: Short traces needed for triage - live payment failures

Hi Aisha,

We started seeing intermittent failures on the payments path this morning. Our SREs requested a short-lived preservation of end-to-end request traces and some ephemeral debug artifacts so they can finish root-cause analysis — specifically: per-request KV cache snapshots and the last 3 minutes of request/response payloads for a subset of request IDs.

We understand your retention policy, but this will be strictly timeboxed and limited to the request IDs attached. Can Redwood preserve those traces for 72 hours while we triage, then confirm secure deletion?

I attached a small SR excerpt with the request IDs. Please advise required form/approvals and who on your side needs to sign off (security, product). We’re blocked on rolling the payment fix without these traces.

Thanks,
Luke
Luke Barnes
SRE Lead, FinProd

Attachments: SR-9876-trace-sample.txt (text)
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Luke Barnes <luke@finprod.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Short traces needed for triage - live payment failures

Hi Luke — thanks for the note and the SR excerpt. Apologies for the disruption.

We can potentially do a limited preservation, but we need to route through our retention-exception flow so security can assess scope and approve a timebound hold. To speed things up:
- Please confirm the explicit request IDs (I see a short list in SR-9876; re-attach if needed).
- Confirm the exact artifacts required (KV snapshot, request/response bodies, logs, anything else).
- Confirm the requested preservation window (you suggested 72 hours) and why that length is necessary.

Soojin — can you advise the minimum info you need to approve a temporary hold? Rishi — if we get sign-off, what’s the fastest way to snapshot only the named request IDs and mark them for deletion after the window?

I’ve attached our preservation form for you to review; if FinProd signs it we can accelerate the internal approvals.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: preserve-request-form.pdf (pdf)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Luke Barnes <luke@finprod.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T13:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Short traces needed for triage - live payment failures

Aisha / Luke — quick security checklist from my side:

1) Narrow scope: list exact request IDs and time window (we prefer sub-minute windows and explicit IDs rather than broad retention).
2) Purpose: short justification of why the traces are required (RCA / fraud analysis / regulatory artifact).
3) Timebox: we typically approve 24–72 hours depending on sensitivity; please specify the rationale for the requested duration.
4) Handling: confirm no customer PII will be exported off-platform and that FinProd’s team will only access via read-only session logs we provision.

If the above are met, I can approve a 48–72 hour hold for this incident. Rishi, please prepare the snapshot plan and indicate rollback steps.

Soojin
Soojin Lee
Security & Privacy, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Luke Barnes <luke@finprod.com>
Date: 2027-04-23T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Short traces needed for triage - live payment failures

On Fri, Apr 22, 2027 at 13:30, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Aisha / Luke — quick security checklist from my side:
>
> 1) Narrow scope: list exact request IDs and time window (we prefer sub-minute windows and explicit IDs rather than broad retention).

Thanks — technical plan below. I confirmed with infra: we can produce a scoped snapshot for named request IDs without changing global retention via our trace-retain API. Steps: 

1) Create a preserve job tied to the SUP ticket (SUP-9876) that enumerates request IDs.
2) The job will copy three artifacts into a locked bucket with encryption: kv-cache-snapshots, request-bodies (redacted, see #4), and runtime logs.
3) Access will be controlled via a short-lived read-only role; FinProd SREs can access through a monitored session (we will log all reads).
4) We will run automated PII redaction filters on payloads — anything flagged will be redacted and reviewed with FinProd before release.
5) The preserve job will stamp an expiry timestamp (default 72h unless security requests shorter) after which automated deletion runs and we produce a deletion certificate to both parties.

ETA: we can spin up the preserve job in ~3 hours once I have: (a) explicit request IDs, (b) confirmation of 72h window, and (c) Soojin approval.

Rishi
Principal Infra SW Eng, Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Luke Barnes <luke@finprod.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-24T15:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Short traces needed for triage - live payment failures

Thanks all — finalizing plan.

Luke — we received the explicit request IDs (from SR-9876) and confirm the artifacts (KV snapshots + request/response bodies + last-3-min logs). You asked for 72 hours; Soojin has tentatively approved up to 72 hours pending confirmation that PII will be redacted before any export. FinProd confirms they will only access via the monitored read-only session we provide and will not export raw payloads.

Next steps (MUTUAL ACTION PLAN):
- Luke (FinProd): confirm in-reply that FinProd will not export raw payloads and agrees to the preserve form terms.
- Soojin (Security): final approval to proceed with a 72-hour hold after redaction step (please reply-all with approval).
- Rishi (Infra): start the preserve job once Soojin approves; notify SUP-9876 when snapshot is live and provide access window details.

We’ll attach the deletion certificate to the ticket once the automatic cleanup completes. Thank you for the quick coordination — hoping this gets the SREs unstuck.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
